questions.q: Which of the following diagrams best represents the relationship among Mammals, Dogs and Cats?
o: A large circle (Mammals) containing two smaller circles (Dogs and Cats) that do not touch each other
Three circles that all overlap one another
A circle (Dogs) inside a circle (Cats), which is inside a circle (Mammals)
Three separate circles, none inside another
questions.e: Dogs and Cats are different kinds of mammals, so each is wholly inside Mammals. No dog is a cat, so those two circles are separate.

questions.q: Which of the following diagrams best represents the relationship among Tigers, Animals and Plants?
o: Three circles that all overlap one another
Three separate circles, none inside another
One circle (Tigers) inside Plants, with Animals separate
One circle (Tigers) inside another (Animals), with a third (Plants) separate from both
questions.e: Every tiger is an animal, so Tigers lies inside Animals. No animal is a plant, so Plants stays completely apart.

questions.q: In a class of 40 students, 25 like tea, 20 like coffee and 5 like neither. How many students like both tea and coffee?
questions.e: Students who like at least one drink: 40 − 5 = 35. Both = 25 + 20 − 35 = 10.

questions.q: Which of the following diagrams best represents the relationship among Women, Teachers and Doctors?
o: Teachers and Doctors overlapping, with Women completely separate
A circle (Women) containing both Teachers and Doctors, which do not touch
Three separate circles, none inside another
Three circles, each overlapping the other two
questions.e: Some women are teachers, some are doctors, and a person can be a teacher and a doctor as well. So all three pairs of circles overlap.

questions.q: Which of the following diagrams best represents the relationship among Apples, Fruits and Red things?
o: Apples and Red things both inside Fruits, separate from each other
Fruits inside Apples, with Red things overlapping Apples
One circle (Apples) inside another (Fruits), with a third (Red things) overlapping both
Three circles that all overlap one another, none inside another
questions.e: Every apple is a fruit, so Apples lies inside Fruits. Some apples are red, and some red things (such as roses) are not fruits, so Red things overlaps both circles.

questions.q: The table gives the number of students in each region of a Venn diagram of three subject groups: English, Maths and Science. How many students study Maths?
questions.e: Maths includes: only Maths 15, English and Maths only 12, Maths and Science only 8, and all three 9. Total = 15 + 12 + 8 + 9 = 44.

questions.q: In a group of 60 people, 35 play cricket, 30 play football and 18 play both games. How many people play exactly one of the two games?
questions.e: Only cricket = 35 − 18 = 17. Only football = 30 − 18 = 12. Exactly one game = 17 + 12 = 29.

questions.q: In a town of 100 families, 60 take newspaper A, 50 take B and 40 take C. Also, 25 take both A and B, 20 take both B and C, 15 take both A and C, and 5 take none of the three. How many families take exactly one newspaper?
questions.e: Families taking at least one: 95. So 95 = 60 + 50 + 40 − 25 − 20 − 15 + x gives x = 5 taking all three. Only A = 25, only B = 10, only C = 10, so exactly one = 45.

questions.q: Of 80 employees, 48 know Java, 40 know Python and 30 know C. Also, 20 know Java and Python, 15 know Python and C, 12 know Java and C, and 5 know all three languages. How many employees know exactly two of the three languages?
questions.e: Exactly two = (20 − 5) + (15 − 5) + (12 − 5) = 15 + 10 + 7 = 32. The 5 who know all three are counted in each pair total, so they are removed from each.

questions.q: Which arrangement of circles best represents the following statements? All engineers are graduates; some graduates are teachers; no engineer is a teacher.
o: Teachers inside Graduates, with Engineers overlapping Teachers
Engineers inside Graduates, with Teachers completely separate from Graduates
Engineers and Teachers both inside Graduates and overlapping each other
Engineers inside Graduates; Teachers overlapping Graduates but not touching Engineers
questions.e: Engineers must lie wholly inside Graduates. Teachers must share part of Graduates, yet stay clear of Engineers, so it overlaps Graduates only in the part outside Engineers.
